first.rationale: The two measured declines this quarter are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and memory_86 and memory_31 are the two inherited findings that directly address exactly those funnel stages, so the single available slot is best spent there. I want the archived records for memory_86 and memory_31 specifically because they are the load-bearing evidence for my intended action and because they are the ones most likely to have degraded in transmission: memory_31 is the oldest record (day 12) and its claim of a 'durable' first-week lift needs its original horizon checked, while memory_86 reports completion-rate and time-to-value gains without stating whether downstream retention or revenue quality was measured at all. Improved completion is not the same as improved qualified revenue, and I should not assume the original experiment tested the latter. I am deliberately not chasing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 is the one inherited memory carrying an explicit harm signal (materially reduced 30-day retention) and an explicit instruction not to generalize it, which cuts directly against the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Reacting to competitive pressure with the one tactic already known to damage retention would be trading the objective for the symptom. Referral incentives (memory_57) are sound but target established customers, which is not where the current deterioration is; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment showing no measured decline. Downstream value risk is real and I am flagging it: cutting required signup fields can degrade lead qualification data, which is precisely what feeds the demo-request path memory_44 credits with superior pipeline quality, so a self-serve activation win could quietly erode enterprise pipeline. Shortening onboarding can also front-load a completion metric while pushing confusion later, inflating a proxy without moving revenue. I therefore want a standard experiment with retention and qualified-revenue readouts held alongside completion and activation, not a broad rollout on the strength of proxy lifts. If verification shows either memory measured only short-horizon proxies, I will keep the action but narrow scope and instrument for downstream effects rather than treating the inherited claim as settled; if memory_31's durability claim does not survive the archive, activation_messaging (memory_91) becomes the stronger fallback.

final.rationale: Verification largely supported the intended direction and sharpened it. exp_86 came back stronger than the compressed memory suggested: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and critically 30-day retention +3%. That last figure was absent from the inherited summary and is the single most relevant number here, because it means the onboarding win is not a proxy inflation that decays downstream. It is the only inherited result showing a positive retention signal alongside a funnel gain, which aligns it directly with the sustainable-qualified-revenue objective. exp_31 also confirmed but with meaningful caveats the summary had smoothed over: retention was -1%, not neutral, and the effect is explicitly SMB-only and not replicated on other segments. The word 'durable' in memory_31 was doing more work than the source record supports. So I am running the onboarding-flow shortening as the primary intervention rather than signup-field cutting. This resolves the downstream risk I flagged earlier: field-cutting at signup is the variant that would have degraded lead qualification data and threatened the demo-request pipeline quality that memory_44 depends on, and it is also the variant carrying the small negative retention drag and the narrower segment warrant. Shortening the onboarding flow addresses both quarterly declines directly, since onboarding completion is the measured -4% and improved time-to-value feeds the -6% activation gap, without touching the enterprise qualification path. Residual uncertainty I am not papering over: exp_86 did not report qualified revenue at all, so the revenue link is inferred from the retention and time-to-value gains rather than measured. That is why this stays a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout, and why I will instrument qualified revenue and enterprise pipeline quality alongside completion and activation rather than reading completion as success. I continue to reject promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing; memory_73 carries an explicit retention harm and an explicit do-not-generalize instruction, and matching a price attack with the one tactic known to damage retention would sacrifice the actual objective to relieve the symptom. Referral incentives and enterprise sales-assist target segments showing no current deterioration. If the readout shows completion rising without movement in activation or qualified revenue, that is a signal the inherited finding does not transfer to present conditions, and activation_messaging per memory_91 becomes the next candidate rather than a wider rollout of this one.
